messages:
incident-bot: PAGERDUTY · SEV2 · potential cross-tenant KV-cache reads detected in dedicated pool dp-us-west-3. Customer impacted: Cryptek (enterprise VPC). Please acknowledge. (thread 2065531122)

alex_k: acked — I'm oncall for infra, taking lead. :eyes: Can folks post the initial detection logs?

maria_ops: Cryptek reported that their embeddings endpoint returned vectors that matched another customer's dataset. We saw prefix collision traces in the gateway logs around 2026-03-14T23:05Z. Sample trace id: trace-0a3b7c.

priya_reliability: timeline: 23:04:55 - Cryptek alert; 23:05:12 - our anomaly detector flagged unusual KV hit rates for prefix "crypt-embed-" mapping to pool dp-us-west-3; 23:06:01 - automated scrub job attempted to evict stale prefixes but returned 500s.

sam_runtime: initial hunch is KV prefix namespace leak: some code path used a non-tenant-scoped key when writing to our global KV cache. Could be a hot key collision after a model rollout.

alex_k: immediate mitigation options: 1) drain dp-us-west-3 and route Cryptek to a fallback pool; 2) apply emergency routing ACL to isolate their tenant prefix; 3) evict suspicious prefixes from KV cache. Which has lowest blast radius?

maria_ops: eviction first is least disruptive. We can run a targeted evict for keys matching `crypt:*` from the shared kvcache. If eviction doesn't cleanly succeed, fallback to draining.

priya_reliability: agree. I'm running a dry-run evict to identify hit counts: `redis-cli -h kvcache-usw3 --scan --pattern "crypt:*" | wc -l` -> shows 12 keys matched across 3 shards.

sam_runtime: Post the exact evict command you plan to run. We should rotate the prefix in Cryptek's routing on success.

maria_ops: Running now (taking a snapshot before):
```
# snapshot
redis-cli -h kvcache-usw3 --scan --pattern "crypt:*" > /tmp/crypt-keys-2065531122.txt
# targeted delete
cat /tmp/crypt-keys-2065531122.txt | xargs -n1 -I{} redis-cli -h kvcache-usw3 DEL {}
```

maria_ops: snapshot saved to /tmp/crypt-keys-2065531122.txt. Starting deletes.

jamie_support: Pinged Cryptek (AE on call: @sales-ae) to inform them we're investigating and will mitigate within the hour. They reported partial readback of another customer's document ids — asked for examples, provided trace-0a3b7c.

sales-ae: Cryptek is very sensitive; legal is on standby. Please confirm root-cause signal before telling them anything beyond "mitigating".

sam_runtime: delete returned 0 for 4 keys, 1 for 8 keys. After delete, run a verification scan: `redis-cli -h kvcache-usw3 --scan --pattern "crypt:*" | wc -l` -> returns 0.

priya_reliability: KV delete success confirmed at 23:12:08Z. However, gateway logs still show occasional cross-tenant read hits; looks like some requests are being routed to a cached prefix resolved earlier (local LRU copies on workers). Need to flush local worker caches (in-memory) as well.

alex_k: Ok do we have a safe command to evict local caches without killing long-lived worker processes? We prefer not to restart everything.

sam_runtime: We have an in-proc cache invalidation endpoint on the runtime: POST /admin/cache/invalidate with JSON body `{ "prefix": "crypt" }`. I'll call it against pool dp-us-west-3 worker set.

sam_runtime: executing: `for host in $(cat dp-usw3-workers.txt); do curl -s -X POST http://$host:8090/admin/cache/invalidate -d '{"prefix":"crypt"}'; done` -> all workers returned 200 OK.

priya_reliability: After worker invalidation, hit rates fell back to baseline. Telemetry: cross-tenant read rate dropped from 0.8% to 0.001% within 3 min.

alex_k: Good. Next actions: 1) run routing rules audit for dp-us-west-3 to ensure tenant-scoped keys are enforced; 2) create a canary to reproduce end-to-end in staging; 3) prepare customer-facing summary for Cryptek (ops+legal review). Assigning tasks.

maria_ops: Assigned task - I'll run the routing rules audit. Query I'm running: `SELECT * FROM route_rules WHERE pool='dp-us-west-3' AND match LIKE '%prefix%';` (from our config DB). Early result shows one legacy rule mapping `embed-*` to dp-us-west-3 that doesn't include tenant guard.

priya_reliability: That legacy rule is likely culprit. It was introduced in 2025-11 during a performance rollback. We should mark it deprecated and add tenant-scoped condition `tenant_id IS NOT NULL`.

jamie_support: For customer comms — draft note: "We detected a small set of cached keys in our shared cache associated with your tenant that could have been served to other customers. We have removed those keys, invalidated runtime caches, and are investigating root cause. No evidence so far of exfiltration beyond the example you reported." Please don't send until legal signs off.

sales-ae: Acknowledged — I'll loop in legal. Keep comms high level.

sam_runtime: immediate infra follow-ups: open PR to remove legacy route and add tenant guard; hardening of cache write path to include tenant namespace enforcement. I'll push the PR and request an expedited review.

alex_k: Also add a short-term autoscrub job to run hourly to detect keys that don't match tenant scoping. We'll run for 24h. Maria please run the scrub job config.

maria_ops: Scrub job scheduled: hourly for next 24h. Filters: keys with prefixes matching `embed-*` without tenant tag. Results will land in ops S3 bucket for 7d.

priya_reliability: Postmortem owner? I'll own the reliability postmortem and coordinate with runtime and product for remediation.

alex_k: Great. Final status for now: mitigation performed (targeted KV deletes + worker cache invalidation), customer notified internally, routing rule identified as likely root cause. No further cross-tenant hits observed after 23:18Z. I'm keeping the thread open for updates and PR links.

incident-bot: Incident status updated -> Mitigated. Pager cleared at 2065531360.

jamie_support: saving notes for handoff: escalated to legal, AE notified, PR link will be posted here when ready. Cryptek asked for timeframe on remediation — told them ~48-72h for full fix and postmortem.

sam_runtime: PR created: github.com/redwood/repo/pulls/8349 — adds tenant guard and unit tests for cache writes. Requesting expedited review from @priya_reliability and @alex_k.

priya_reliability: Reviewing now. Will merge after one more +1. Also scheduling a canary deploy to staging tomorrow morning to validate no perf regression.

alex_k: Thanks all. I'll file incident card and link this thread. If anything new appears, re-pager.

sales-ae: Cryptek legal asked for a record of deleted keys and timelines; Jamie, please prepare a sanitized export from /tmp/crypt-keys-2065531122.txt and the scrub job logs.

jamie_support: on it. Export will be uploaded to secure share after legal OK.

maria_ops: closing hands: metrics remain nominal. Will monitor for 48h.

alex_k: closing the live mitigation handoff, leaving the postmortem to Priya. Thanks everyone. :tada:
